subject: general
question: What will happen if bubbles of air are sent through lime water taken in a container?

options.text: The solution will turn milky due to insoluble suspension of Calcium carbonate
The temperature will rise due to an exothermic reaction
The solution will foam and froth
The solution will instantly red as reacts with lime

solution:
The correct answer is '**The solution will turn milky due to insoluble suspension of Calcium carbonate'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• If bubbles of air are sent through lime water taken in a container then the solution will turn milky due to insoluble suspension of Calcium carbonate.
 
• On bubbling Carbon dioxide in clear lime water in small amounts, the clear solution turns milky due to the formation of calcium carbonate .
